mainTopic: Levels of disqualification for a כהן, and the head, back, eyebrow, nose, and eye blemishes
overview: The גמרא first sets out three levels of disqualified כהן. A true מום makes his עבודה invalid. Being 'not equal among the seed of אהרן' (שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן) breaks a Torah עשה, but the עבודה still counts. מראית העין is only a rabbinic ban. Next the גמרא explains the odd head and neck shapes in the משנה. It also explains the dispute about a hunchback and רבא's two versions of which bald כהן is disqualified. רבי יוחנן rules that bald, dwarf, and leaky-eyed כהנים are disqualified by Torah law, against a ברייתא that follows רבי יהודה. A new משנה defines the גבן, and the גמרא settles a contradiction from a ברייתא and explains 'two spines' as a crooked spine. Another משנה lists the חרום and many eye blemishes. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא on nose blemishes, where the חכמים tell רבי יוסי he went too far, a reply that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: How does a true blemish differ from being 'not equal'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between a כהן with a real מום and a כהן who is שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between a blemish and one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. Both kinds of כהן cannot serve, so what is the difference between them? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some features in the משנה are full-fledged מומין, which disqualify both people and animals. Others disqualify a כהן only because he looks different from normal כהנים. If both are banned from the עבודה, the גמרא wants to know whether the two categories ever lead to a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between (formula asking for the practical difference)
One who is not equal (normal-looking) among the descendants of אהרן

phrases.english: What difference is there between
a blemish and one who is not equal
among the seed of Aaron?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין מוּמָא לְשֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the comparison of the categories of disqualification
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical legal difference between a מום and שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן

steps.title: A true blemish ruins the service; 'not equal' does not
steps.stepSummary: The difference is חילול עבודה. A כהן with a מום who serves ruins (מחלל) the עבודה, based on the פסוק 'מום בו ולא יחלל'. A כהן who is not equal does not ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference regarding profaning the service. A blemish profanes the service, as it is written: 'He has a blemish, that he not profane.' One who is not equal among the seed of Aaron does not profane the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. If a כהן with a real מום does the עבודה anyway, it does not count. If a כהן who is merely 'not equal' does it, it still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מום בו ולא יחלל' links a real מום directly to profaning the עבודה. That פסוק speaks about a true מום. It does not cover the weaker category of 'not equal'. So both are forbidden to serve, but only a true מום makes the service invalid after the fact (בדיעבד).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a key distinction. Being forbidden to serve (לכתחילה) is not the same as having your service invalid after the fact (בדיעבד).

phrases.english: There is a difference regarding profaning the service:
a blemish profanes the service,
as it is written: 'He has a blemish, that he not profane,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״א:כ״ג

phrases.english: one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron
does not profane the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מום invalidates the עבודה (from 'מום בו ולא יחלל'); שאינו שוה does not

steps.title: How does 'not equal' differ from a merely apparent blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference there is between שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן and a כהן who is disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron and one disqualified because of appearance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second comparison question. This time it compares 'not equal' with an even lighter category, things that only look like a blemish. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither of these two kinds of כהן invalidates the עבודה, so the difference from step 2 does not help here. The גמרא needs some other legal difference to justify treating them as two separate categories.

keyTerms.meaning: Mere appearance (looks like a blemish but is not one)

phrases.english: What difference is there between one who is not equal
among the seed of Aaron,
and one disqualified because of appearance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison to a third category
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between שאינו שוה and מראית העין

steps.title: 'Not equal' violates a Torah positive command
steps.stepSummary: The difference is an עשה. A כהן who is not equal and serves anyway transgresses a Torah prohibition stated as a positive command. A כהן disqualified for מראית העין does not, because his disqualification is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer. Serving while 'not equal' breaks a Torah עשה. Serving with only an apparent blemish does not, because that ban comes from the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three levels of disqualification. A true מום ruins the עבודה. 'Not equal' does not ruin the עבודה, but serving still breaks a Torah עשה. מראית העין is only a rabbinic disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment (here, a prohibition derived from a positive command)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. (1) מום: Torah ban, and it invalidates the עבודה. (2) שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן: Torah עשה, but the עבודה remains valid. (3) מראית העין: rabbinic only.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שאינו שוה violates a Torah עשה; מראית העין is only rabbinic

steps.title: Defining the pointed head and the turnip head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains two head shapes from the משנה. A כילון has a head shaped like a barrel cover: narrow on top and wide below. A לפתא has a head like the top of a turnip: wide on top and narrow below.
steps.simpleTranslation: כילון: whose head resembles a barrel cover. 'לפתא': whose head resembles the top of a turnip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to defining terms from the משנה, one by one. It starts with two head shapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each odd word is explained by comparing it to an everyday object. That way the learner can picture the shape. The two shapes are opposites: one is narrow on top and the other is wide on top.

keyTerms.meaning: A pointed head, like a barrel cover

phrases.english: Kilon: whose head resembles a barrel cover,
'Turnip-like': whose head resembles
the top of a turnip,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section explaining the משנה's list of blemishes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כילון is a head shaped like a barrel cover; לפתא is a head shaped like the top of a turnip

steps.title: A ברייתא adds: the neck stands in the middle of the head
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds another detail of this blemish: the neck sits in the middle of the head, rather than toward the back as it does on a normal person.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And his neck stands in the middle of his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds one more detail about the turnip-shaped head (לפתא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a normal person the neck is toward the back of the head. Here the head sticks out equally all around the neck. That uneven look is what makes him 'not equal'.

phrases.english: It was taught: And his neck stands
in the middle of his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא detail to the head-shape definitions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The neck is set in the middle of the head

steps.title: Defining the hammer head, the dented front, and the flat back
steps.stepSummary: A מקבן has a head like a hammer, with the forehead sticking out. שקוט means the head is sunken in front. סקיפת means the back of the head looks as if a piece was cut off, as people say 'שקיל פיסא', 'a piece was taken'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מקבן: whose head resembles a hammer. 'And whose head is שקוט': in front. 'And סקיפת': in back, as people say: a piece was taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues defining head shapes from the משנה. For one of them it uses a popular saying to explain the odd word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שקוט is a dent in the front of the head, and סקיפת is a flatness at the back. The word סקיפת is explained as a shortened form of the phrase 'שקיל פיסא', meaning a piece was taken off.

keyTerms.meaning: Back of the head looks cut off

phrases.english: Makkavan: whose head resembles a hammer,
'And whose head is indented': in front of it,
'And sekifat': at the back of it,
as people say: a piece was taken.
phrases.notes: סקיפת is read as a contraction of שקיל פיסא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining the משנה's head blemishes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקבן is a hammer-shaped head; שקוט is a dent in front; סקיפת is a flattened back of the head

steps.title: A ברייתא on the sunken neck and the long narrow neck
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that a כהן whose neck is שקוט or שמוט is also disqualified. שקוט means the neck is pressed down and hidden between the shoulders. שמוט means the neck is long and narrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And his neck is שקוט or שמוט. 'שקוט': it is pressed in. 'שמוט': it is long and drawn out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds two neck blemishes, then explains each word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that the same word שקוט now describes the neck, and it means something new: a short neck sunk between the shoulders. שמוט is the opposite problem, a neck that is too long and thin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שקוט of the head (a dent in the front of the head, step 7) with שקוט of the neck (a short neck sunk between the shoulders).

phrases.english: It was taught: And one whose neck is short or narrow.
'Short': whose neck is pressed in and hidden,
'Narrow': whose neck is long and drawn out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds neck blemishes from a ברייתא and defines them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A neck that is short and sunken (שקוט) or long and narrow (שמוט) also disqualifies a כהן

steps.title: The hunchback: where the dispute really lies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's dispute about a hunchback. It explains that everyone agrees a hump with bone in it disqualifies the כהן. They argue only about a hump with no bone: the רבנן say he is 'not equal among the seed of אהרן', and רבי יהודה says it is just a lump of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And those with humps: רבי יהודה (says they are fit, and the רבנן say they are disqualified).' If the hump has a bone in it, everyone agrees he is disqualified. They argue only when there is no bone. One opinion holds that he still does not look like the rest of the seed of אהרן. The other opinion holds that it is just a lump of flesh and means nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, the dispute about a כהן with a hump. It then narrows down exactly what רבי יהודה and the רבנן are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא takes the case where there is bone out of the argument, because everyone agrees that kind of hump disqualifies. That leaves only a hump of flesh in dispute. The רבנן look at appearance: he still looks different from other כהנים. רבי יהודה looks at substance: a lump of flesh is not a real blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: People with humps on their backs
Everyone agrees; there is no dispute
He is not equal (does not look the same) as the rest of the descendants of אהרן

steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to Step 4. The reason 'not equal among the seed of אהרן' is a real category of disqualification, separate from a mere concern about how things look.

phrases.english: And those with humps, Rabbi Yehuda etc.
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה: רבי יהודה deems them fit; the רבנן deem them disqualified.

phrases.english: Where there is a bone in it (the hump),
everyone agrees that it disqualifies.
Where they disagree is when there is no bone in it:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר — הָא אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: this person is not equal among the seed of Aaron,
phrases.notes: The רבנן, who disqualify.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר — קִרְקוּרָא דְּבִישְׂרָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: it is merely a lump of flesh.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה, who deems him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the head and neck blemishes (Steps 5-8) to the next item in the משנה: the hunchback.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hump with bone disqualifies according to everyone. A hump of flesh alone is disputed: the רבנן disqualify because he is not equal among the seed of אהרן, and רבי יהודה allows him because it is just flesh.

steps.title: רבא limits the bald priest's disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a קרח is disqualified. רבא says this applies only when he is missing the row of hair in the back but has it in the front. If he has hair in the back, he is fit. He is certainly fit if he has hair in the back but none in the front.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The bald man is disqualified.' רבא said: This was taught only when he has no hair in the back but does have hair in the front. But if he has hair in the back, he is fit. All the more so if he has hair in the back and none in the front.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a bald כהן is disqualified. רבא then explains exactly which kind of baldness the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא narrows the ruling. Only an odd pattern disqualifies: missing hair in the back while keeping it in the front. If there is hair in the back, he is fit. Losing hair in the front only is the normal way older men go bald, so he is fit 'all the more so'.

keyTerms.meaning: A bald man; in the משנה, one who lacks the row of hair around his head
'They only taught this when...': a formula that limits a ruling to a specific case
In the back of his head / in the front of his head

phrases.english: The bald man is disqualified.
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו
phrases.english: They taught this only when he has no (hair) in the back
but he has (hair) in the front,
but if he has (hair) in the back, he is fit,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and all the more so if he has in the back and does not have in the front.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה: the bald כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרח is disqualified only when he lacks hair in the back but has it in the front. With hair in the back he is fit, and he is certainly fit if only his front is bald.

steps.title: A second version of רבא's statement, on the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some attach רבא's statement to the end of the משנה, 'if he has (the row of hair), he is fit.' In this version, he is fit only when he has hair in the back and not in the front. If he has hair both front and back, he is disqualified. He is certainly disqualified with hair in front only, or with no hair at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רבא's statement on the end of the משנה: 'And if he has (the row of hair), he is fit.' רבא said: This was taught only when he has hair in the back and none in the front. But if he has hair both in the back and in the front, he is disqualified. All the more so if he has hair in the front and none in the back, or no hair at all. Then he is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different tradition of רבא's statement. In this version, רבא is explaining the end of the משנה, the case where the כהן is fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבא is now limiting the ruling that he is fit, the result flips. Only the normal balding pattern (hair in the back, none in front) is fit. Hair both front and back now disqualifies, apparently because it looks unusual. Front-only hair or total baldness disqualifies all the more so.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (a different version)
The latter clause or end of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רבא disagree about a כהן who has hair both in front and in back. In the first version he is fit. In the second version he is disqualified. Both versions agree that hair in the back only means fit.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא on the bald כהן. Version 1 (on the רישא): only 'no hair in back, hair in front' disqualifies. Version 2 (on the סיפא): only 'hair in back, none in front' is fit, and every other pattern disqualifies.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the latter clause,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: 'and if he has (the row of hair), he is fit.'
phrases.notes: Quotation of the end of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he has (hair) in the back and does not have in the front,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֲרָיו בֵּין לְפָנָיו — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: but if he has (hair) both in the back and in the front, he is disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְפָנָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו,
phrases.english: and all the more so one who has in the front and does not have in the back,
and one who has none at all, that he is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different tradition of רבא's statement from Step 10. Attaching it to the סיפא produces a stricter result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a כהן with hair in the back and none in the front is fit. Hair both front and back, hair in front only, or no hair at all all disqualify.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: bald men, dwarves, and leaky-eyed priests are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that bald כהנים, dwarves, and כהנים with leaky eyes are disqualified. His reason is that they are not equal among the seed of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Bald men, dwarves, and men with leaky eyes are disqualified, because they are not equal among the seed of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי יוחנן listing three kinds of כהנים who may not serve. This also sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three are grouped under one reason: they look different from other כהנים. This is the same reason the רבנן used for the hunchback in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Men whose eyes constantly leak or tear

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The bald men, the dwarves, and those with leaky eyes are disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן.
phrases.english: because they are not equal among the seed of Aaron.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַקַּרְחָנִין וְהַנַּנָּסִין וְהַזַּבְלְגָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new list from an אמורא, using the same 'not equal among the seed of אהרן' reasoning seen in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bald כהנים, dwarves, and כהנים with leaky eyes are disqualified because they are not equal among the seed of אהרן.

steps.title: Why say it? We already learned bald men and dwarves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. A משנה already teaches that a bald man is disqualified, and another משנה teaches that a dwarf is disqualified. So why did he need to say these?
steps.simpleTranslation: Bald men: we already learned that! Dwarves: we already learned that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that two of the three items on רבי יוחנן's list are already written in משניות. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not supposed to simply repeat what a משנה already says. Our משנה taught the קרח, and a later משנה (45b) teaches the dwarf. So the challenge asks what new point רבי יוחנן is adding. Only the leaky eyes are not challenged here.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.english: Bald men: we already learned it!
phrases.notes: In our משנה: 'the bald man is disqualified.'

phrases.english: Dwarves: we already learned it!
phrases.notes: In a later משנה (45b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 12 as repeating what משניות already teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's inclusion of bald men and dwarves in his list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: both cases are already explicit in משניות, so stating them again seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Leaky eyes is new, and the others are disqualified by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case of זבלגנין is not in any משנה. It also explains that רבי יוחנן repeated bald and dwarf so we would not think they are disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach us about the כהן with leaky eyes, since no משנה mentions it. And he repeated the others because you might have said they are disqualified only because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. It explains why רבי יוחנן's statement is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer has two parts. First, the זבלגנין case is completely new, because no משנה teaches it. Second, for bald and dwarf כהנים, רבי יוחנן's reason ('not equal among the seed of אהרן') shows they are disqualified by Torah law (דאורייתא), and not just by a rabbinic concern about appearance (מראית העין).

keyTerms.meaning: People whose eyes constantly leak or tear
You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea we need to avoid)
How something looks to onlookers; here, a disqualification based only on appearance

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate points here. Leaky eyes is a brand-new ruling. Bald and dwarf are not new rulings. They are repeated to teach how serious the disqualification is: Torah law, not just appearance.

phrases.english: Leaky-eyed ones, he needed to teach us,
phrases.notes: No משנה mentions this case.

phrases.english: and (he repeated the others) lest you say
(they are disqualified only) because of appearance.
phrases.notes: In other words, only a rabbinic disqualification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 that רבי יוחנן's statement is redundant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement adds new information: a new case, plus the level of the disqualification.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think bald and dwarf כהנים are disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are disqualified by Torah law because they are not equal among the seed of אהרן, and leaky eyes is a new case.

steps.title: The משנה states it openly when the reason is appearance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Whenever the reason is only מראית העין, the תנא says so openly, as with fallen eyelashes. So nobody would mistake the bald and dwarf cases for appearance-only.
steps.simpleTranslation: But whenever the reason is appearance, the תנא teaches it openly: 'One whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified because of appearance'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 14. There was no real risk of the mistake that answer described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's pattern is to add the words 'because of appearance' when that is the reason. The bald and dwarf cases have no such label, so we already know they are full disqualifications. That means רבי יוחנן still seems unnecessary for them.

phrases.english: But surely, anywhere
that (the reason) is because of appearance,
he (the תנא) teaches it explicitly,
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is the corrected reading.

phrases.english: 'and one whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified
because of appearance'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִשּׁוּם מַרְאִית הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one might think bald and dwarf כהנים are disqualified only because of appearance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה labels appearance-only cases explicitly. Since these cases have no label, no one would make that mistake.

steps.title: Maybe the label was said once and meant for all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might think the תנא wrote 'because of appearance' only once, and meant it for the whole list.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he taught it once, and the same applies to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier answer. Someone could still have read the bald and dwarf cases as appearance-only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the משנה might not repeat the label for each case. Saying it once could cover the whole list. So רבי יוחנן was needed to show the bald and dwarf cases are full Torah disqualifications.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
he taught one (explicitly),
and the same is true for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggests a possible misreading of the משנה's structure that רבי יוחנן needed to block.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single 'because of appearance' label might cover the whole list.
steps.terutzMaskana: So רבי יוחנן clarifies that bald and dwarf are full Torah disqualifications.

steps.title: The משנה repeats the label each time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that defense. The תנא actually repeats 'because of appearance' each time it applies, as with missing teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But whenever it applies, he repeats and teaches it again: 'One whose teeth were removed is disqualified because of appearance'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the defense from step 16. It points to a second place where the משנה repeats the label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the label covered the whole list, the תנא would not need to say it again. But he does say it again for missing teeth (44a). This proves he labels each appearance-only case on its own, so the unlabeled bald and dwarf cases were never in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes back and teaches it

phrases.english: But surely, anywhere
where there is a need to repeat and teach it,
he does repeat and teach it:
'and one whose teeth were removed is disqualified
because of appearance'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִיהְדָּר וּמִיתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one 'appearance' label covers the whole list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה repeats the label for teeth, so it labels each case separately. The unlabeled cases are clearly not appearance-only.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was rejecting a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier approach. It explains that רבי יוחנן was rejecting a ברייתא that calls bald, dwarf, and leaky-eyed כהנים fit by Torah law, disqualified only because of appearance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant to exclude what a ברייתא teaches: 'Bald ones, dwarves, and leaky-eyed ones are fit. They only said they are disqualified because of appearance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us the גמרא is giving up the earlier answer and offering a new one. רבי יוחנן was arguing against a specific ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about appearance-only did not come from reading the משנה. It came from a real ברייתא that rules this way. רבי יוחנן's reason, 'not equal among the seed of אהרן', shows he rejects that ברייתא. For him these are Torah-level disqualifications.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject (a different view)
As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling is not redundant. He disagrees with a ברייתא that says bald, dwarf, and leaky-eyed כהנים are fit by Torah law and disqualified only because of מראית העין. For him they are fully disqualified.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same blemish can be a Torah disqualification or only a rabbinic one about appearance, depending on which source you follow.

phrases.english: Rather, (it is) to exclude that which is taught,
as it is taught (in a ברייתא):
'The bald, the dwarves, and the leaky-eyed are fit,
and they only said disqualified
because of appearance.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the defense of steps 14 and 16 after the challenge in step 17, and offers a new answer to step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies an opposing source that רבי יוחנן's statement rejects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following the ברייתא, these כהנים are fit by Torah law and disqualified only because of appearance.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן rules they are disqualified by Torah law, against that ברייתא.

steps.title: Who taught this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who taught the ברייתא that calls these כהנים fit. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding the author connects the ברייתא to a known opinion. This shows the view comes from an established sage.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is this תנא (teacher of the משנה or ברייתא)?

phrases.english: Who is this תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who wrote the ברייתא cited in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that bald, dwarf, and leaky-eyed כהנים are fit by Torah law.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, who includes bald priests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. He learns from the word הכהנים that bald כהנים are included in the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, 'the כהנים' comes to include bald ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יהודה as the author. It quotes his teaching from a verse to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the extra word 'הכהנים' in the verse ('the sons of אהרן, the כהנים') as including bald כהנים in the Temple service. This fits his view in step 9, where he calls a boneless hump just a lump of flesh. רבי יוחנן's 'not equal among the seed of אהרן' follows the רבנן instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The כהנים' (a word in the verse, read as including more people)

steps.whatToRemember: The lenient ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view: bald כהנים are fit by Torah law. רבי יוחנן rules against him.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה,
as it is taught: רבי יהודה says:
'The priests' comes to include the bald ones.
phrases.notes: ויקרא א׳:ח׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who learns from 'הכהנים' that bald כהנים may serve.

steps.title: The משנה's first definition of a gibben
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that a כהן with no eyebrows, or with only one eyebrow, is the גבן mentioned in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he has no eyebrows, or has only one eyebrow, that is the גבן the תורה talks about.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It defines the Torah's blemish גבן as a כהן who has no eyebrows or only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists גבן among the blemishes that disqualify a כהן from serving. The תנא קמא of the משנה links the word גבן to eyebrows (גבינין). In his view, the blemish is missing eyebrows.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish listed in the Torah that disqualifies a כהן
That is stated in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Here גבן is NOT the usual meaning 'hunchback.' The תנא קמא connects it to גבינין, eyebrows.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he has no eyebrows,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְּבִין אֶחָד —
phrases.english: or he has only one eyebrow —
that is the gibben stated in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לוֹ גְּבִינִין, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְּבִין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion of bald, dwarf, and leaky-eyed כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן with no eyebrows or one eyebrow is the גבן of the Torah and is disqualified.

steps.title: Two other definitions of a gibben
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says a גבן has eyebrows that lie flat. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says a גבן has two backs and two spines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: it is one whose eyebrows lie down over his eyes. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: it is one who has two backs and two spines.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings two more opinions about what a גבן is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא still connects the blemish to eyebrows, but his case is eyebrows that are too long and droop. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס connects גבן to the back (גב) instead. His wording, 'two spines,' will be challenged in step 25.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
one whose eyebrows lie flat.
phrases.notes: The parentheses and brackets show a text correction: read שגביניו, 'his eyebrows.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת.
phrases.english: one who has two backs and two spines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds alternative definitions to the תנא קמא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: drooping eyebrows. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: two backs and two spines.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns the case of no eyebrows from the word 'or'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the word גבן really means 'no eyebrows.' A ברייתא says גבן means many eyebrows, and that 'no eyebrows' is learned from the word 'או.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does גבן mean one who has no eyebrows? Raise a contradiction: 'גבן' means one who has many eyebrows. From where do we know about one with no eyebrows, or only one eyebrow? The verse says: 'Or a גבן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'no eyebrows' is the plain meaning of גבן. The ברייתא says the plain word גבן means a כהן with too many eyebrows. In the ברייתא, 'no eyebrows' is only added through the extra word 'או' (or).

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction (between two sources)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But does gibben mean one who has no eyebrows?
And raise a contradiction:
'Gibben' — one who has many eyebrows;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ גְּבִינִין, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְּבִין אַחַד — מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: one who has no eyebrows, or only one eyebrow — from where?
The verse states: 'Or a gibben.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא's definition from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that 'no eyebrows' is the meaning of גבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines plain גבן as many eyebrows and learns 'no eyebrows' only from the extra word 'או.' So 'no eyebrows' is not the plain meaning of גבן.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה means the derivation from 'or a gibben'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's phrase 'that is the גבן stated in the Torah' means it is learned from the דרשה of 'או גבן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is the exposition of 'Or a גבן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was not claiming that the word גבן alone means 'no eyebrows.' It meant that this case is included in the Torah through the phrase 'או גבן,' just as the ברייתא says. So the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: An exposition, a teaching drawn from a verse
Or (the extra word that includes more cases)

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is the exposition of 'or a gibben.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: זֶהוּ מִדְרָשׁ אוֹ גִּבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the plain word גבן means 'no eyebrows.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means 'no eyebrows' comes from the דרשה of 'או גבן,' matching the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: Plain גבן means many eyebrows. The cases of no eyebrows or one eyebrow are added by the word 'או.'

steps.title: Can a creature with two spines live?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a living כהן could have two backs and two spines, since רב rules that such a creature is not considered viable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says, etc. Does this mean such a creature can live? But it was stated: if a woman or an animal miscarries a creature with two backs and two spines, רב said: for a woman, it is not a child; for an animal, it is forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's definition from step 22. It uses a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished כהן is a living person. רב treats a creature with two backs and two spines as unable to live. A woman who miscarries it does not count as having given birth. If an animal gives birth to it, it is forbidden to eat, like a טרפה. So how can a living כהן have this condition?

keyTerms.meaning: A child (a birth that counts in halacha)

steps.confusionAlert: The heading quotes רבי דוסא, but the question is really about the next opinion in the משנה, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, who spoke of two spines.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה section. The question targets רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

phrases.english: Is this to say that he can live?
But it was stated:
one who miscarries a creature

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: that has two backs and two spines,
and Rav said:
in a woman — it is not an offspring;
in an animal — it is forbidden to eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new difficulty, about רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's definition of גבן as having two backs and two spines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that a creature with two backs and two spines is not viable. A blemish of a living, serving-age כהן cannot be a non-viable condition.

steps.title: רב: it means a crooked spine
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא already asked רב this question. רב answered that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס means a crooked spine, which only looks like two spines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא already raised this contradiction to רב. רב said to him: Are you שימי? Rather, it means one whose spine is crooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reporting that רב himself solved this problem. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not mean two real spines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Are you שימי?' expresses surprise that a sharp student would ask this. 'Two spines' describes how a badly crooked spine looks. Such a person can live, so it is a real blemish for a כהן, and רב's ruling about non-viable creatures still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He already raised this contradiction to him
Are you שימי? (an expression of surprise)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's 'two backs and two spines' is not literal. It means a crooked spine that looks like two, which a living person can have.

phrases.english: Already raised this contradiction
Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya to Rav,
and he said to him: Are you Shimi?!
Rather, it refers to one whose spine is crooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר רְמָא נִיהֲלֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Two backs and two spines' meant two real spines, a condition no one can live with.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a crooked spine that looks like two. A person can live with this, so it is a valid blemish.

steps.title: New משנה: the חרום is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a חרום is disqualified and defines him as one who can paint both eyes at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חרום is disqualified. Who is a חרום? Someone who can paint both of his eyes in one stroke.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It names a new blemish, the חרום, and defines it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition is a practical test. Normally the nose bridge separates the eyes, so you cannot paint both with one brushstroke. If you can, the nose must be sunk flat, and that is the blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
A blemished כהן whose nose is sunk (ויקרא כ״א:י״ח)
As one, in a single stroke

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not describing a man who wears eye makeup. Painting both eyes in one stroke is just a test that shows the nose is flat.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The ḥarum is disqualified.
phrases.notes: Disqualified from serving in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Who is a ḥarum?
One who can paint both his eyes as one.
phrases.notes: Because his nose is sunk, nothing blocks the brush between his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of the גבן ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרום, defined as one who can paint both eyes in one stroke, is disqualified.

steps.title: משנה lists eye blemishes and the case of fallen eyelashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists eye blemishes that disqualify a כהן. It says one whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified only because of appearance.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both eyes are too high or too low, or one is high and one is low, or he sees the downstairs room and the upstairs at the same time, or he cannot look at the sun, or his eyes are different from each other, or his eyes tear constantly, he is disqualified. One whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a list of eye blemishes. It ends with fallen eyelashes, which disqualify only because of appearance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most items on the list are real Torah-level blemishes in the eyes' position, vision, or condition. Fallen eyelashes are different: the Torah does not disqualify for them, but חכמים did, because the כהן looks blemished (מראית העין).

keyTerms.meaning: A ground-floor room and an upper story. He sees both at once, as with crossed or misaligned vision.
One who cannot look at the sun
One whose two eyes are different from each other
Appearance. Disqualified rabbinically because it looks like a blemish.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'מפני מראית העין' applies only to the last case, fallen eyelashes. The earlier cases are full Torah-level blemishes.

phrases.english: Both his eyes are above,
phrases.notes: Set too high on the face.

phrases.english: or both his eyes are below,

phrases.aramaic: עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: one eye above and one eye below,

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּיה כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: he sees the room and the upper story as one,
phrases.notes: His eyes look in two directions at the same time.

phrases.english: those unable to look at the sun,
and one whose eyes are different, and one whose eyes tear constantly,
and one whose eyelashes have fallen out —
is disqualified due to the appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of face and eye blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These eye defects disqualify a כהן. Fallen eyelashes disqualify only rabbinically, because of appearance.

steps.title: A ברייתא widens חרום to include other nose defects
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says חרום means a sunken nose. It adds other nose defects through the word 'או'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'חרום' means a כהן whose nose is sunk. If his nose is turned up short, blocked, or drooping too long, where do we learn that? The verse says 'או חרום', 'or a חרום'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא. The ברייתא defines חרום and uses the word 'או' to add more nose blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word חרום covers only a sunken nose. The extra word 'או' extends the blemish to any badly shaped nose: too short, blocked, or drooping. This matches the pattern we saw with גבן in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows again that the word 'או' in this list of blemishes is used to widen each category.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
'Ḥarum' means one whose nose is sunk.
If his nose retreats upward,
his nose is blocked,
or his nose droops, from where do we know?
The verse states: 'Or a ḥarum.'
phrases.notes: The word 'או' adds every nose blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines the משנה's term חרום and widens it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sunken nose is a חרום. Other nose defects are added from 'או חרום'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits חרום to the eye-painting case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says חרום means only one who can paint both eyes in one stroke.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A חרום is only someone who can paint both his eyes in one stroke.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a narrower definition of חרום than the תנא of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a nose counts only if it is sunk so completely that both eyes can be painted at once. A nose that is only somewhat sunk would not qualify. His wording matches the משנה's definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Is only. This is a limiting phrase.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
A ḥarum is only
one who can paint both his eyes as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֵין חָרוּם אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a narrower definition than the ברייתא's first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one whose nose is so sunk that both eyes can be painted at once is a חרום.

steps.title: The חכמים say רבי יוסי went too far
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that רבי יוסי's definition is too extreme.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You have gone too far.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי's narrow definition. Their full explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their claim is that limiting חרום to such an extreme case is going too far. A nose that is clearly sunk, even if not that flat, should already count. Their reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: You have gone too far, you have exaggerated

phrases.english: They said to him: You have gone too far,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד (44a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to רבי יוסי's narrow definition.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי's limit of חרום to the eye-painting case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His definition is too extreme and leaves out noses that are clearly sunk.
